record.paper_title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: For a fixed closed Riemannian manifold M, does there exist a function f_M from possible lengths to nonnegative integers, depending only on the geometry and topology of M, such that every finite connected embedded closed geodesic net on M of total length L has at most f_M(L) balanced vertices, where closed means the boundary or unbalanced vertex set is empty and degree-2 balanced vertices are suppressed?

evidence.quote: we are going to consider below only geodesic nets where all balanced vertices have degree ≥ 3.

Problem 2.0.4 (Becker-Kahn). Let M be a closed Riemannian manifold. Is there a function fM (depending on geometry and topology of M) such that each closed geodesic net on M of length L has at most fM(L) (balanced) vertices?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a fixed closed (compact, without boundary) Riemannian manifold. A finite embedded graph $\Gamma \subset M$ whose edges are smooth geodesic arcs is called a geodesic net. A vertex $v \in \Gamma$ is called balanced if the sum of the unit tangent vectors at $v$ along the edges meeting $v$ equals zero in $T_vM$; otherwise it is called unbalanced (a boundary vertex). One says $\Gamma$ is a closed geodesic net if it has no unbalanced vertices. By convention, degree-2 balanced vertices are suppressed (so that two collinear geodesic arcs are treated as a single edge), and only vertices of degree $\geq 3$ are considered. Define the total length $L(\Gamma)$ as the sum of the lengths of all edges.

Question: Does there exist a function $f_M : [0,\infty) \to \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$, depending only on the geometry and topology of $M$, such that every finite connected embedded closed geodesic net $\Gamma$ on $M$ with $L(\Gamma) \leq L$ has at most $f_M(L)$ balanced vertices?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2024–2025) on geodesic nets continues to investigate the number of balanced vertices in low-boundary-vertex cases (e.g., three or four boundary vertices in the plane) and constructs nets with increasing numbers of balanced vertices, but no source establishes a length-dependent bound on the number of balanced vertices for closed geodesic nets on a general closed Riemannian manifold. The Becker–Kahn problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of a balanced vertex in geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Studies existence of balanced vertices for geodesic nets with three boundary vertices, indicating the broader question on bounding balanced vertices remains active.
status_evidence.claim: Active research as of 2024 on balanced-vertex counts in geodesic nets, with no global bound known.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs planar geodesic nets with four boundary vertices and many balanced vertices (e.g., 25), suggesting balanced vertex count can grow.
status_evidence.claim: Researchers are still constructing nets to probe balanced-vertex counts; problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Nets: Some Examples and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the Becker–Kahn problem on bounding the number of balanced vertices of a closed geodesic net of bounded length as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is recorded as open.
